subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.11 published dist missing reentrancy guard - reply session initialization conflicted

question: Should maintainers publish a stable release that supersedes affected v2026.6.11 with the current reply-session initialization fixes in the bundled dist?
rationale: The source fixes are already on main, but the remaining problem is the latest stable npm/GitHub artifact; release inclusion and package promotion require maintainer authority rather than a new source-only repair PR.

options.title: Publish fixed stable package
options.body: Cut or promote a stable release that includes the current reply-session fixes, then verify the npm tarball dist contains the reentrant writer/session-accessor behavior.

options.title: Wait for scheduled stable train
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical tracker until the next planned stable release ships and can be artifact-verified.

options.title: Close only after prerelease validation
options.body: Use a beta as validation signal, but do not close this stable-release issue until the stable channel no longer points users at the affected package.

recommendation.title: Publish fixed stable package
recommendation.body: Cut or promote a stable release that includes the current reply-session fixes, then verify the npm tarball dist contains the reentrant writer/session-accessor behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The release tag/current-main stability history makes this the best available routing candidate for the package-promotion decision.
